name: Saudi Arabia
summary: Banks are licensed and supervised by the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) under the Banking Control Law, with SAMA's instructions published in the SAMA Rulebook. Suspicious transaction reports go to the General Directorate of Financial Investigation (the Saudi FIU), the Capital Market Authority regulates securities business, SDAIA supervises personal data protection and ZATCA receives FATCA and CRS reports. Explicit training duties come from the AML and CTF implementing regulations, SAMA's AML/CTF Guide (training before starting work and annual knowledge testing), the 2025 Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules, the Counter-Fraud and Cyber Security Frameworks, the compliance and conduct principles, and mandatory professional certificates for front-line and credit staff. This map covers conventional banking only.

regulators.name: Saudi Central Bank
regulators.role: Licenses, regulates and supervises banks, including AML/CTF, conduct, consumer protection, cyber and fraud requirements; publishes the SAMA Rulebook.

regulators.name: General Directorate of Financial Investigation (Saudi FIU)
regulators.role: Receives and analyses suspicious transaction reports from financial institutions under the AML and CTF laws.

regulators.name: Capital Market Authority
regulators.role: Regulates securities markets and capital market institutions, including investment arms of banking groups; not covered in detail by this map.

regulators.name: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority
regulators.role: Competent authority for the Personal Data Protection Law and national data governance rules.

regulators.name: Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority
regulators.role: Competent authority for FATCA and CRS reporting by Saudi financial institutions.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | AML Awareness under the AML Law and SAMA AML/CTF Guide
programs.why: The implementing regulation of the 2017 AML Law requires ongoing employee training programmes as part of every bank's AML controls. SAMA's AML/CTF Guide adds that all staff are trained before starting work and repeatedly afterwards, that knowledge is tested at least once a year and that training records are kept.

references.title: Implementing Regulation to the Anti-Money Laundering Law
references.issuer: Government of Saudi Arabia (SAMA Rulebook copy)
references.note: Internal AML policies, procedures and controls of financial institutions must include ongoing employee training programmes, alongside staff screening, a senior-level compliance officer and independent audit.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Training on AML/CTF policies for all current staff and for new staff before they start, repeated over time; deeper training for due diligence staff; specialised training for compliance and internal audit; board, directors and managers included; knowledge testing at least annually and records of training kept.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering Law (Royal Decree No. M/20)
references.issuer: Government of Saudi Arabia (SAMA Rulebook copy)
references.note: Banks must adopt AML policies, procedures and controls approved by senior management; the implementing regulation lists what they must cover, including training.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Combating Terrorist Financing under the CTF Law
programs.why: The implementing regulations of the Law on Combating Terrorism Crimes and its Financing require continuing employee training as part of each bank's CFT policies, and SAMA's AML/CTF Guide applies the same induction, refresher and annual testing expectations to terrorist financing.

references.title: Implementing Regulations of the Law of Combating Terrorist Crimes and its Financing
references.note: CFT policies and procedures of financial institutions must include continuing employee training programmes, staff screening and an independent audit procedure.

references.title: Law on Combating Terrorism Crimes and its Financing (Royal Decree No. M/21, as amended)
references.issuer: Government of Saudi Arabia (SAMA Rulebook copy)
references.note: Financial institutions must have and apply policies, procedures and controls against terrorist financing; their content is set by the implementing regulations. Amended by Royal Decree M/142 of 2020.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Training on AML/CTF policies for all current staff and for new staff before they start, repeated over time; deeper training for due diligence staff; specialised training for compliance and internal audit; board, directors and managers included; knowledge testing at least annually and records of training kept.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Proliferation Financing and UN Sanctions under SAMA TFS Rules
programs.why: SAMA's 2025 Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules require role-based training for staff applying UN Security Council measures, including those on weapons of mass destruction proliferation and its financing, and SAMA's December 2025 business risk guidance brings proliferation financing into the bank-wide risk assessment.

references.title: Rules for the Implementation of Targeted Financial Sanctions
references.note: Risk-based training, tailored by role, for all staff who apply the rules, including simulation exercises for specialists, in-person workshops for the sanctions unit, refresher sessions, comprehension testing and focused awareness for senior management and the board.

references.title: Guidance on Assessing Business Risks Related to Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing, and Proliferation Financing
references.note: Sets how financial institutions assess ML, TF and PF risks arising from their business, as part of the risk-based approach.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Know Your Customer under SAMA Account Opening Rules
programs.why: SAMA's Account Opening Rules forbid banks from placing tellers or customer service staff in post before they complete KYC, AML/CFT and professional ethics courses, and require continuing training that covers the rules in depth.

references.title: Account Opening Rules
references.provision: Chapter II, Rule 9 (Training as a Key Principle for these Rules)
references.note: Banks may not assign teller or customer service staff until they have attended courses on KYC, AML/CFT and banker ethics, and must run continuing on-the-job training covering these rules.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Customer Due Diligence under the SAMA AML/CTF Guide
programs.why: Due diligence is required by the AML Law and detailed in Section 3 of SAMA's AML/CTF Guide; Section 11 requires more comprehensive and detailed training for the employees who carry out due diligence, matched to the bank's risks.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Training on AML/CTF policies for all current staff and for new staff before they start, repeated over time; deeper training for due diligence staff; specialised training for compliance and internal audit; board, directors and managers included; knowledge testing at least annually and records of training kept.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Sets out SAMA's expectations for identifying and verifying customers and beneficial owners and for relying on third parties.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Enhanced Due Diligence under the SAMA AML/CTF Guide
programs.why: The AML Law requires enhanced measures for higher-risk relationships and high-risk countries, and Section 4 of SAMA's Guide describes them; staff who apply EDD must be able to do so, but no EDD-specific course is prescribed beyond the general due diligence training duty.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Covers enhanced measures for higher-risk customers, including politically exposed persons.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering Law (Royal Decree No. M/20)
references.issuer: Government of Saudi Arabia (SAMA Rulebook copy)
references.note: Enhanced due diligence proportionate to risk for persons from high-risk countries, and application of countermeasures set by the national AML committee.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Beneficial Ownership under the SAMA AML/CTF Guide
programs.why: Banks must identify and verify the natural persons who ultimately own or control customers; staff handling legal-person customers need the knowledge to apply these rules, though no separate training is prescribed.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Explains why ownership must be traced to natural persons and links to the implementing regulation provisions on identifying beneficial owners.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Politically Exposed Persons under the SAMA AML/CTF Guide
programs.why: The AML Law and SAMA's Guide require reasonable steps to identify PEPs, their family and close associates and to apply enhanced measures to high-risk PEP relationships; competent staff are needed but no PEP-specific course is prescribed.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Requires reasonable measures to determine whether a customer or beneficial owner is a PEP and enhanced measures for high-risk PEP relationships.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Sanctions Screening under SAMA Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules
programs.why: SAMA's 2025 TFS Rules require screening to be done by trained staff and make training and awareness a required element of the sanctions policy, with role-based training, simulations, refresher sessions, testing and a record of all training delivered.

references.title: Rules for the Implementation of Targeted Financial Sanctions
references.note: Risk-based training, tailored by role, for all staff who apply the rules, including simulation exercises for specialists, in-person workshops for the sanctions unit, refresher sessions, comprehension testing and focused awareness for senior management and the board.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Targeted Financial Sanctions: Freezing and Unfreezing under SAMA TFS Rules
programs.why: The TFS Rules require training on freezing and lifting freezes, alert handling, confidentiality and the legal consequences of non-compliance, delivered in person to the sanctions unit and by e-learning to other relevant units, with focused awareness for the board.

references.title: Rules for the Implementation of Targeted Financial Sanctions
references.note: Risk-based training, tailored by role, for all staff who apply the rules, including simulation exercises for specialists, in-person workshops for the sanctions unit, refresher sessions, comprehension testing and focused awareness for senior management and the board.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Suspicious Transaction Reporting to the Saudi FIU
programs.why: The AML Law requires prompt reports to the General Directorate of Financial Investigation and bans tipping off. SAMA's compliance principles require public-facing staff to be periodically reminded of suspicious reporting duties, and the AML/CTF Guide requires all staff to know their duties and the penalties for failure.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering Law (Royal Decree No. M/20)
references.issuer: Government of Saudi Arabia (SAMA Rulebook copy)
references.note: Suspicions must be reported promptly to the General Directorate of Financial Intelligence; directors and employees must not disclose that a report has been or will be made.

references.title: Principles of Compliance for Commercial Banks Operating in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
references.note: The compliance unit must help senior management run an annual training and awareness programme for all employees, train new joiners on the compliance requirements of their work before they start, and periodically remind public-facing staff of sales, AML/CTF, due diligence and suspicious reporting rules.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Board-approved internal reporting procedures, a channel for staff to raise suspicions and measures to prevent tipping off.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Unusual Transaction Monitoring under the SAMA AML/CTF Guide
programs.why: Banks must continuously monitor transactions and identify unusual activity, and SAMA's Guide expects staff to be equipped to recognise it; the monitoring duty itself does not set a separate training requirement.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.provision: Section 7: Monitoring of Transactions and Activities
references.note: Expects risk-based monitoring systems and procedures that identify unusual and suspicious transactions for review and reporting.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | ML/TF Typologies and Emerging Trends under the SAMA AML/CTF Guide
programs.why: SAMA's Guide requires AML/CTF training to draw on real cases and to include updates and new ML/TF methods, so that staff can recognise transactions and typologies and know how to respond.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Training on AML/CTF policies for all current staff and for new staff before they start, repeated over time; deeper training for due diligence staff; specialised training for compliance and internal audit; board, directors and managers included; knowledge testing at least annually and records of training kept.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Correspondent Banking under the SAMA AML/CTF Guide
audience: Correspondent banking and financial institutions teams
programs.why: The AML Law and SAMA's Guide require information gathering, risk assessment and senior approval before entering correspondent relationships; staff managing them need specialised knowledge but no separate training is prescribed.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Measures to take before and during correspondent relationships, including understanding the respondent's business, supervision and AML/CTF controls.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | AML/CFT Risk-Based Approach and Business Risk Assessment
programs.why: Banks must assess and document their ML/TF risks and, since SAMA's December 2025 guidance, assess business risks including proliferation financing; the Guide expects training to enable staff to apply the risk-based approach.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Requires a documented, comprehensive assessment of customer, product, geographic and channel risks as the basis of the risk-based approach.

references.title: Guidance on Assessing Business Risks Related to Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing, and Proliferation Financing
references.note: Method for assessing inherent and residual business risks for ML, TF and PF.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | AML Record Keeping under the AML Law and SAMA Guide
programs.why: Banks must keep transaction and due diligence records for at least ten years and make them available to authorities; staff handling records need to know these rules, but no specific course is prescribed.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Records must be kept for at least ten years after the relationship ends or the transaction completes, and be available to competent authorities.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering Law (Royal Decree No. M/20)
references.issuer: Government of Saudi Arabia (SAMA Rulebook copy)
references.note: Record-keeping duty for domestic and international transactions and due diligence documents.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | AML for Tellers, Branch and Customer Service Staff
programs.why: SAMA requires tellers and customer service staff to complete KYC and AML/CFT courses before taking up the role, allows AML tasks to be assigned only after accredited AML/CFT courses, and requires periodic reminders of AML and reporting duties for public-facing staff.

references.title: Account Opening Rules
references.provision: Chapter II, Rule 9 (Training as a Key Principle for these Rules)
references.note: Banks may not assign teller or customer service staff until they have attended courses on KYC, AML/CFT and banker ethics, and must run continuing on-the-job training covering these rules.

references.title: Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics in Financial Institutions
references.note: Staff may be given AML/CFT tasks only after attending specialised accredited AML/CFT courses, and the institution must spread AML/CFT knowledge through training and bulletins.

references.title: Principles of Compliance for Commercial Banks Operating in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
references.note: The compliance unit must help senior management run an annual training and awareness programme for all employees, train new joiners on the compliance requirements of their work before they start, and periodically remind public-facing staff of sales, AML/CTF, due diligence and suspicious reporting rules.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | AML/CFT Responsibilities of the Board and Senior Management
programs.why: SAMA's AML/CTF Guide requires training to cover board members, committees, managers and executives and requires directors to know their duties and the penalties for non-compliance; the TFS Rules add sanctions awareness for the board and senior management.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Training on AML/CTF policies for all current staff and for new staff before they start, repeated over time; deeper training for due diligence staff; specialised training for compliance and internal audit; board, directors and managers included; knowledge testing at least annually and records of training kept.

references.title: Rules for the Implementation of Targeted Financial Sanctions
references.note: Risk-based training, tailored by role, for all staff who apply the rules, including simulation exercises for specialists, in-person workshops for the sanctions unit, refresher sessions, comprehension testing and focused awareness for senior management and the board.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | AML/CFT for Compliance and Internal Audit Functions
programs.why: SAMA's Guide requires specialised and adequate AML/CTF training for the compliance function and the independent audit function, and requires a senior-level AML/CTF compliance officer with qualified staff.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Training on AML/CTF policies for all current staff and for new staff before they start, repeated over time; deeper training for due diligence staff; specialised training for compliance and internal audit; board, directors and managers included; knowledge testing at least annually and records of training kept.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.provision: Section 9: Arrangements of AML/CTF Compliance Function
references.note: Requires an independent AML/CTF unit headed by a senior-level officer, with sufficient resources and qualified staff.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Anti-Bribery and Corruption under SAMA Conduct Principles
programs.why: SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics require institutions to fight bribery and corruption and to educate staff on their seriousness and harm, and require staff to report suspected bribery.

references.title: Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics in Financial Institutions
references.provision: Section III.C.2 (Dealing with Bribery and Corruption)
references.note: Institutions must educate staff about the gravity of bribery and corruption; staff must report suspicions and avoid favouritism and abuse of authority.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Fraud Prevention under the SAMA Counter-Fraud Framework
programs.why: SAMA's Counter-Fraud Framework requires an employee fraud training and awareness programme at or soon after onboarding with regular refreshers, knowledge checks, specialised role-based modules and tailored board training. Branch and customer service staff also need fraud awareness material at least every three months.

references.title: Counter-Fraud Framework
references.note: Fraud awareness programme for staff, customers and third parties; employee training at onboarding and at regular intervals, with knowledge checks, specialised training by role, board training and training records.

references.title: Control and Awareness Measures for Branch and Customer Service Employees in Banks Operating in the Kingdom
references.note: Banks must run awareness campaigns on information security and fraud prevention for branch and customer service staff at least every three months and test effectiveness at least every six months.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Regulatory Compliance Awareness under SAMA Compliance Principles
programs.why: SAMA's compliance principles for commercial banks require an annual training and awareness programme for all staff, compliance training for new joiners before they start, and periodic reminders for public-facing staff.

references.title: Principles of Compliance for Commercial Banks Operating in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
references.note: The compliance unit must help senior management run an annual training and awareness programme for all employees, train new joiners on the compliance requirements of their work before they start, and periodically remind public-facing staff of sales, AML/CTF, due diligence and suspicious reporting rules.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Corporate Governance under SAMA Key Principles of Governance
programs.why: SAMA's Key Principles of Governance require qualified board members and committee members with the knowledge to fulfil their duties, and require the board to make sure control functions are resourced and trained; they set no general governance course.

references.title: Key Principles of Governance in Financial Institutions Subject to Saudi Central Bank's Oversight and Supervision
references.note: Board members must be qualified, competent and willing to keep learning; the board must ensure compliance, internal audit and risk management staff are trained and their capabilities developed.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Board Induction under SAMA Key Principles of Governance
programs.why: Each new board member must receive an induction programme on the institution's mission, strategy and activities and a note on the duties of membership.

references.title: Key Principles of Governance in Financial Institutions Subject to Saudi Central Bank's Oversight and Supervision
references.note: Every board member must receive an induction programme on the institution's mission, strategic objectives and activities, with a memorandum on the duties and responsibilities of membership.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Fit and Proper Requirements for Senior Positions
programs.why: Senior position holders need SAMA's prior non-objection and must meet integrity, competence and capability criteria; institutions must also run training to qualify Saudi successors for senior posts.

references.title: Requirements for Appointments to Senior Positions
references.note: Fit and proper criteria (integrity, competence and capability) for senior positions, SAMA non-objection, and a board-approved replacement and succession policy with continuing training for Saudi candidates. The English text is not the latest version.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Code of Conduct under SAMA Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics
programs.why: Banks must adopt a conduct and work ethics policy based on SAMA's principles, explain the principles to staff when they join, and have managers make sure every employee reads and signs them.

references.title: Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics in Financial Institutions
references.note: The principles apply to all staff; managers must ensure they are read, signed and filed, and the institution must explain them to staff on joining.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Whistleblowing under the SAMA Whistle Blowing Policy
programs.why: SAMA's whistleblowing policy requires financial institutions to raise awareness among staff and stakeholders about confidential reporting channels and protection, and to prepare awareness programmes that encourage reporting of violations.

references.title: Whistle Blowing Policy for Financial Institutions
references.note: Institutions must publicise reporting channels, reassure staff about confidentiality and protection from retaliation, and run awareness programmes that encourage reporting.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Financial Consumer Protection under SAMA Principles and Rules
programs.why: SAMA's 2022 Financial Consumer Protection Principles and Rules require banks to train front-line employees who deal with consumers on a regular basis and to make sure they hold the required professional certificates.

references.title: Financial Consumer Protection Principles and Rules
references.note: Front-line staff must be trained regularly and hold the necessary professional certificates covering customer handling, products and SAMA instructions; Rule 15 adds monitoring visits to branches and call centres.

references.title: Ensuring Continuous Fulfilment of the Professional Certification Requirement
references.note: Front-line bank staff must hold the retail banking fundamentals certificate and staff directly involved in granting credit to individuals (and branch managers) the credit adviser certificate, obtained within one year of employment, with at least 90% of the target staff certified.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Responsible Lending: SAMA Credit Adviser Certification
programs.why: SAMA requires bank staff directly involved in granting credit to individuals, and branch managers, to obtain the credit adviser professional certificate within one year of employment, including staff supplied by third parties.

references.title: Ensuring Continuous Fulfilment of the Professional Certification Requirement
references.note: Front-line bank staff must hold the retail banking fundamentals certificate and staff directly involved in granting credit to individuals (and branch managers) the credit adviser certificate, obtained within one year of employment, with at least 90% of the target staff certified.

references.title: Professional Certificates of Financial Institution Employees
references.note: Earlier circular making the retail banking and credit adviser certificates compulsory for front-line, sales, call-centre and customer care staff, including staff supplied by third parties, even if they held older editions.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Complaint Handling under SAMA Consumer Protection Rules
programs.why: SAMA requires a clear and effective complaints mechanism and fair, timely resolution; complaint handlers need to know the rules and SAMACares procedures, but no separate training is prescribed.

references.title: Financial Consumer Protection Principles and Rules
references.note: Institutions must provide a clear complaint mechanism and resolve each complaint fairly, effectively and without delay.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Serving Persons with Disabilities under SAMA Instructions
programs.why: SAMA's instructions for services to persons with disabilities require institutions to prepare a service guide and to train and qualify specialised staff to serve customers with disabilities in an accessible way.

references.title: Instructions for Services Provided to Persons with Disabilities in Financial Institutions
references.note: Institutions must adapt procedures, prepare a guide for serving persons with disabilities and train and qualify specialised staff to do so.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Customer Confidentiality for Branch and Customer Service Staff
programs.why: SAMA requires awareness campaigns at least every three months for branch and customer service staff on confidentiality of customer account information and penalties for breaches, staff testing every six months, and a signed declaration on joining and every year.

references.title: Control and Awareness Measures for Branch and Customer Service Employees in Banks Operating in the Kingdom
references.note: Quarterly awareness campaigns on confidentiality of customer information and SAMA instructions, tests at least every six months, and staff declarations at the start of employment and annually.

references.title: Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics in Financial Institutions
references.note: Staff must keep customer and institution information confidential during and after employment and follow the information security policy.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Debt Collection under SAMA Debt Collection Regulations
programs.why: SAMA's 2025 Debt Collection Regulations and Procedures require a board-approved collection policy and require creditors to make sure their own and third-party collection staff know the policy and can prove it.

references.title: Debt Collection Regulations and Procedures
references.note: Creditors need a written collection policy and must ensure that employees and third parties involved in collection are aware of it, with proof of that awareness.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Retail Banking Professional Certification for Front-Line and Sales Staff
programs.why: SAMA makes the retail banking fundamentals professional certificate compulsory for front-line bank staff, including branch staff and managers, sales and call-centre staff and contracted staff, to be obtained within one year of employment.

references.title: Ensuring Continuous Fulfilment of the Professional Certification Requirement
references.note: Front-line bank staff must hold the retail banking fundamentals certificate and staff directly involved in granting credit to individuals (and branch managers) the credit adviser certificate, obtained within one year of employment, with at least 90% of the target staff certified.

references.title: Professional Certificates of Financial Institution Employees
references.note: Earlier circular making the retail banking and credit adviser certificates compulsory for front-line, sales, call-centre and customer care staff, including staff supplied by third parties, even if they held older editions.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Information Security Awareness for Branch and Customer Service Staff
programs.why: SAMA requires banks to train and qualify branch and customer service staff in information security basics, run awareness campaigns at least every three months, test staff every six months and collect signed policy declarations at joining and yearly; the Cyber Security Framework requires awareness for all staff.

references.title: Control and Awareness Measures for Branch and Customer Service Employees in Banks Operating in the Kingdom
references.note: Training and qualification on essential information security, quarterly awareness campaigns, six-monthly tests and joining and annual declarations for branch and customer service staff.

references.title: Cyber Security Framework
references.note: A cyber security awareness programme for staff, third parties and customers, run periodically through the year and evaluated for effectiveness.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Cyber Security Awareness under the SAMA Cyber Security Framework
programs.why: SAMA's Cyber Security Framework requires an approved cyber security awareness programme for staff, third parties and customers, tailored to target groups, run periodically through the year and evaluated.

references.title: Cyber Security Framework
references.note: Awareness programme covering security measures, roles and responsibilities and emerging threats, run periodically throughout the year for staff, third parties and customers.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Cyber Security Skills Training under the SAMA Cyber Security Framework
programs.why: The Cyber Security Framework requires specialist security training for key roles, the cyber security function, staff who build and maintain information assets and staff involved in risk assessments.

references.title: Cyber Security Framework
references.note: Specialist or security skills training in line with job descriptions for key roles, cyber security staff, developers and maintainers of information assets and risk assessment staff.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Personal Data Protection Law Compliance
programs.why: The Personal Data Protection Law has applied since September 2023 with enforcement from September 2024; SAMA requires financial institutions to align their policies with it and with SDAIA rules. The law and SDAIA texts could not be opened from this environment, so no express training duty was confirmed.

references.title: Adherence to the Personal Data Protection Law and Data Governance Policies, Regulations and Rules
references.note: SAMA directs financial institutions to bring internal policies into line with the PDPL and SDAIA data governance rules, close gaps under a board-approved plan and protect customers' personal data.

references.title: Personal Data Protection Law
references.note: National data protection law issued by Royal Decree M/19 of 1443H and amended by Royal Decree M/148 of 1444H; host not reachable for verification.

references.title: Implementing Regulation of the Personal Data Protection Law
references.note: Implementing regulation published by SDAIA in 2023; host not reachable for verification.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Phishing and Social Engineering Awareness
programs.why: The Cyber Security Framework requires the awareness programme to cover current cyber threats such as spear-phishing and whaling, and SAMA's branch staff measures require awareness of being observed while entering credentials.

references.title: Cyber Security Framework
references.note: The awareness programme must at minimum cover emerging cyber events and threats, citing spear-phishing and whaling as examples.

references.title: Control and Awareness Measures for Branch and Customer Service Employees in Banks Operating in the Kingdom
references.note: Staff must be made aware of shoulder-surfing risks when entering usernames and passwords, and of information security and fraud threats through quarterly campaigns.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | IT Staff Competence under the SAMA IT Governance Framework
programs.why: SAMA's IT Governance Framework requires an annual IT training plan, formal training for existing and new IT staff and contractors, specialist training for critical IT roles and identification of required professional certifications.

references.title: Information Technology Governance Framework
references.note: Annual IT training plan, formal training for IT staff and contractors, specialist training for critical roles and defined professional certifications.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Credit Risk Management under SAMA Rules on Credit Risk Management
programs.why: SAMA requires every bank to run credit risk under a board-approved credit policy, with clear delegation of lending authority, credit administration, risk rating and internal controls. The credit policy must oblige senior management to make sure staff in credit appraisal, administration and review are well trained, and staff assigning internal risk ratings must be trained so ratings are applied consistently.

references.title: Rules on Credit Risk Management
references.note: Board must ensure credit staff have sound expertise; the credit policy must require senior management to keep them well trained; staff assigning risk ratings must be trained.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Liquidity Risk Management and ILAAP under SAMA Guidelines
programs.why: Banks must assess their own liquidity adequacy through an Internal Liquidity Adequacy Assessment Plan, run regular liquidity stress tests and keep a contingency funding plan, alongside the LCR and NSFR rules. No separate course is prescribed, but treasury, ALM and risk staff need working knowledge of the ILAAP and Basel III liquidity standards to run it.

references.title: Guidelines on the Internal Liquidity Adequacy Assessment Plan (ILAAP)
references.note: Sets out what a bank ILAAP must cover, including regular liquidity stress tests and a contingency funding plan; replaces the 1438H version.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book under SAMA IRRBB Rules
programs.why: SAMA applies the Basel IRRBB standard through its own rules and regulatory returns, with Pillar 3 disclosures now set in section 25 of the Pillar 3 framework. Banks must measure and report banking-book rate risk using standardised shock scenarios, which demands competent ALM and risk staff; no express training duty is stated.

references.title: Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB)
references.note: Applies the Basel IRRBB standard in Saudi Arabia and sets the regulatory returns banks must submit.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Capital Adequacy, Basel III and ICAAP under SAMA Rules
programs.why: Banks must hold capital under SAMA final Basel III rules (credit risk framework in force from 1 January 2023) and run an Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Plan that covers all material risks, stress testing and capital planning. These require knowledgeable risk and finance staff and informed senior management, but SAMA does not prescribe a separate course.

references.title: SAMA's Guideline Document on the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Plan (ICAAP)
references.provision: Circular 291000000581, read with circular 321000027835 (Enhancements to the ICAAP)
references.note: Explains how banks build an ICAAP covering material risks, stress tests and capital planning beyond Pillar 1.

references.title: Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk
references.note: SAMA final Basel III credit risk capital framework, effective 1 January 2023, with quarterly reporting of credit RWAs.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Stress Testing under SAMA Rules on Stress Testing
programs.why: SAMA requires banks to run a board-approved stress testing framework with scenarios that fit their risk profile. Senior management must set up a suitable structure and assign qualified people to carry out the tests, a competence duty rather than a training mandate.

references.title: Rules on Stress Testing
references.note: Senior management must design and run the stress testing framework with an appropriate structure and qualified human resources.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Concentration Risk under SAMA Large Exposure Rules
programs.why: The Large Exposure Rules cap exposures to single counterparties and groups of connected counterparties and require their identification and reporting. Credit and reporting staff need to understand connected-party aggregation and exemptions; no express training duty applies.

references.title: Large Exposure (LEX) Rules for Banks
references.note: Sets large exposure limits, connected-counterparty aggregation and reporting requirements based on the Basel large exposures framework.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Outsourcing under SAMA Rules on Outsourcing
programs.why: SAMA's Rules on Outsourcing require banks to manage the risks of outsourcing arrangements; staff who arrange and oversee them need to understand these rules, but the rules set no training requirement.

references.title: Rules on Outsourcing
references.note: Sets risk management, approval and oversight expectations for banks that outsource activities, functions and processes.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Business Continuity under the SAMA BCM Framework
programs.why: SAMA's Business Continuity Management Framework requires a training and awareness programme supporting BCM objectives, with training at least once a year for employees involved in BCM and periodic measurement of its effectiveness.

references.title: Business Continuity Management Framework
references.note: BCM training and awareness programme; annual training for employees involved in BCM and periodic effectiveness checks.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Recovery and Resolution Planning under the SIFI Law
programs.why: The Law of Systemically Important Financial Institutions lets SAMA require a recovery plan within 180 days, covering capital and liquidity recovery options, critical activities and governance, and provides for resolution planning. Those who own the plan must understand it, but the law sets no training duty.

references.title: Systemically Important Financial Institutions Law
references.note: Requires designated institutions to prepare recovery plans with prescribed contents and supports resolution planning.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Credit Policy Compliance under SAMA Rules on Credit Risk Management
programs.why: Every bank must have a board-approved credit policy, filed with SAMA and reviewed at least every three years, that covers lending authority, collateral, exposure limits and staffing. One required element is that senior management keeps credit staff well trained, so staff who apply the credit policy need training on it.

references.title: Rules on Credit Risk Management
references.note: Lists the mandatory contents of the credit policy, including a requirement that credit staff are well trained and periodically rotated.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Problem Loans and NPL Management under SAMA Rules
programs.why: SAMA rules require early warning systems, an NPL strategy, an independent workout unit, restructuring principles and collateral standards. Banks must staff the workout unit with people who have the needed analytical, legal and financial skills, which is a competence duty; the companion guidelines give practical detail.

references.title: Rules on Management of Problem Loans
references.note: The workout unit must be independent of loan origination and staffed with people who have the required skills.

references.title: Guidelines on Management of Problem Loans
references.note: Practical guidance on early warning signals, NPL strategy, workout plans and restructuring principles.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Loan Classification, Provisioning and IFRS 9 Impairment under SAMA Rules
programs.why: SAMA rules set loan classification categories, minimum provisioning and an independent credit review system, with prudential returns on classification and provisioning. Expected-loss impairment follows IFRS 9 as applied by SAMA since 2018. Staff must apply these consistently, but no express training duty exists.

references.title: Loan Classification, Provisioning and Credit Review
references.note: Sets loan classification, minimum provisioning, an independent credit review function and the related prudential returns.

references.title: IFRS 9 (International Financial Reporting Standard-9)
references.note: IFRS 9 applies in Saudi Arabia from 1 January 2018; SAMA adopted the Basel transitional treatment for accounting provisions.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Credit Bureau Reporting under the Credit Information Law
programs.why: Banks that are members of licensed credit bureaus must obtain consumer consent before enquiries, report accurate data at least weekly, correct errors, flag disputed items and keep bureau data confidential. Staff handling credit data need to know these duties; the law sets no training requirement.

references.title: Credit Information Law
references.note: Governs the collection and exchange of consumer credit information by licensed credit bureaus and their members.

references.title: Implementing Regulations of Credit Information Law
references.note: Lists member duties: consent, accurate weekly updates, error correction, dispute flags and confidentiality.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Consumer Financing under SAMA Regulations for Consumer Financing
programs.why: The Regulations for Consumer Financing set disclosure, contract, fee, balance transfer and collections rules for bank lending to individuals. Creditors must run structured training for all new staff and consumer finance product knowledge training for marketing, sales and customer service staff, and give collections staff a code of conduct.

references.title: Regulations for Consumer Financing
references.note: Requires structured training for new staff and product knowledge training for consumer finance sales and service staff.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Real Estate Finance for Individuals under SAMA Instructions
programs.why: When offering home finance to individuals, banks must have a qualified employee explain the product and its risks, and before an offer expires must assign a separate qualified credit adviser well versed in real estate finance to explain terms, risks and any repricing. This is an express competence requirement for named roles under the Real Estate Finance Law framework.

references.title: Instructions When Offering Real Estate Finance Products for Individuals
references.note: Product explanations must come from a qualified employee, and a separate qualified credit adviser must brief the client before the offer expires.

references.title: Real Estate Finance Law
references.note: Framework law for real estate finance supervised by SAMA.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Account Opening and Documentation under SAMA Account Opening Rules
programs.why: The Account Opening Rules set document requirements for residents, non-residents and juristic persons and are amended often. Banks may not assign tellers or customer service staff until they have attended KYC, AML/CFT and professional conduct courses, must run continuing on-the-job training, and must include extensive training on the Rules themselves.

references.title: Account Opening Rules
references.note: No teller or customer service assignment before KYC, AML/CFT and ethics courses; ongoing training must cover the contents of the Rules.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Dormant and Unclaimed Accounts under SAMA Account Opening Rules
programs.why: Accounts become dormant after 24 months without customer activity and unclaimed after 60 months, with dual-control reactivation, restrictions on withdrawals and a staged customer contact policy. These are part of the Account Opening Rules, which require extensive training on their contents.

references.title: Account Opening Rules
references.note: Defines dormant and unclaimed accounts, controls on reactivation and contact duties; rule 9 requires training on the Rules. The English text notes the Arabic version holds the latest 2023 amendment.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Wire Transfers under the SAMA AML/CTF Guide
programs.why: Domestic and cross-border wire transfers in any currency, including cover payments, must carry complete originator and beneficiary information under Article 10 of the AML Law and Article 68 of the CTF Law. Payments staff must know these duties; general AML training covers them but no separate course is set.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Guide: Section 14 Wire Transfer
references.note: Requires originator and beneficiary information on all wire transfers, including card and device-initiated transfers.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Payment Systems under the Payments Law and SARIE Rules
programs.why: The Law of Payments and Payment Services gives SAMA oversight of payment systems such as SARIE and mada and lets it set competency standards for staff of operators and providers. Licensed banks providing payment services are exempt from licensing but must follow the provisions SAMA applies to them, and SARIE indirect participation has its own rules. No express staff training duty applies to banks.

references.title: Law of Payments and Payment Services
references.note: Sets the legal basis for payment systems and payment service providers and SAMA power to set staff competency standards.

references.title: Implementing Regulations of Payments and Payment Services Law
references.note: Licensed banks providing payment services need no separate licence but must comply with the provisions SAMA specifies.

references.title: Rules of Saudi Arabian Riyal Interbank Express Indirect Participation
references.note: Conditions for indirect participation in SARIE through a direct participant bank.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Credit Card Operations under SAMA Rules of Issuance and Operation of Credit Cards
programs.why: New credit card rules issued in June 2025 cover issuance, agreements, reimbursement, statements, transactions, unauthorised use reporting and fees. They set no express training duty, but card and service staff must apply them correctly.

references.title: Rules of Issuance and Operation of Credit Cards
references.note: Current card rules on issuance, agreements, statements, unauthorised use and fees.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | ATM and POS Controls under SAMA Instructions
programs.why: SAMA requires daily ATM balancing on its form, prompt refund of surplus cash to customers, monthly surprise counts by internal audit, dual control of ATM cash and codes, and one-week settlement of ATM and POS claims. Staff in charge must know these controls; no training duty is stated.

references.title: Internal Controls on ATMs and POSs
references.note: Sets daily balancing, dual control, surprise audits and claim settlement timelines for ATMs and POS terminals.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Agent Banking under the SAMA Regulation of Agent Banking
programs.why: Banks using agents must assess agents as fit and proper and must train the agents' employees before any agent banking activity starts and throughout the contract. Minimum topics include products, KYC, customer data protection and complaints, fraud and counterfeit detection, AML/CFT, equipment and reconciliation, and obtaining the Retail Banking Professional Foundation Certificate.

references.title: Regulation of Agent Banking in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
references.note: Requires training of agent staff before activities begin and throughout the contract, with set minimum topics including the RBPFC.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Remittance Operations under SAMA Rules Governing Banks' Remittance Centers
programs.why: Bank remittance centres must verify customers and beneficial owners, record full transfer details, and be led by a manager with relevant qualifications and banking experience. The guide requires banks to give remittance centre employees appropriate and continuous training so they can serve customers professionally.

references.title: Guide to Rules Governing Banks' Remittance Centers
references.note: Requires appropriate and continuous training for remittance centre employees and a qualified centre manager.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Prevention of Sexual Harassment at Work
programs.why: Saudi Arabia's Anti-Harassment Law of 2018 makes harassment an offence and is reported to require employers to adopt preventive measures in the workplace, but the official text on the legislation and labour ministry portals could not be opened from this environment, so no training duty was confirmed.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | IFRS 9 Implementation under SAMA Guidance
programs.why: IFRS 9 applies to Saudi banks from 1 January 2018. SAMA issued industry guidance on governance and ownership across finance, risk and treasury, classification and measurement, past-due definitions, impairment and disclosures, and set national discretions for the capital transition. Finance and risk staff must be competent in it; no training mandate is stated.

references.title: IFRS 9 (International Financial Reporting Standard-9)
references.note: Confirms IFRS 9 application from 2018, summarises SAMA guidance topics and sets transitional capital treatment.

references.title: IFRS 9-Financial Instruments
references.note: Earlier circular introducing the industry implementation guidance on IFRS 9 governance, impairment and disclosures.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Pillar 3 Disclosures under the SAMA Pillar 3 Framework
programs.why: SAMA revised Pillar 3 framework, effective 1 January 2023, sets templates, frequency, assurance and guiding principles for public risk disclosures, including IRRBB, liquidity, leverage and remuneration. Preparers need detailed knowledge, but the framework sets no training duty.

references.title: Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework
references.note: Effective 1 January 2023, with first templates as at 31 March 2023, and requires assurance of Pillar 3 data.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | FATCA Reporting under the Saudi-US Intergovernmental Agreement
programs.why: Saudi banks report US accounts to ZATCA under the FATCA intergovernmental agreement, so onboarding and reporting staff need to understand self-certification and due diligence; ZATCA's pages could not be opened from this environment, and SAMA's 2014 FATCA circular is marked no longer applicable.

references.title: Information Exchange (FATCA and CRS)
references.note: ZATCA page for automatic exchange of financial account information; host not reachable for verification.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Common Reporting Standard under ZATCA Guidance
programs.why: Reporting Saudi financial institutions must apply CRS due diligence and report to ZATCA; staff collecting self-certifications need to understand the rules. ZATCA's guidance could not be opened from this environment, so no training duty was confirmed.

references.title: CRS Guidance Notes Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
references.note: ZATCA guidance on CRS obligations of reporting Saudi financial institutions; host not reachable for verification.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Open Banking under the SAMA Open Banking Framework
programs.why: SAMA issued the Open Banking Framework in November 2022, starting with account information services and moving to payment initiation. Banks had to make internal systems, procedures and policies ready to connect with licensed providers, and SAMA began licensing fintechs for open banking in March 2026. Staff need knowledge of the framework, consent and data rules; no training mandate is stated.

references.title: Emphasizing the Importance to Be Prepared to Link with Open Banking Service Providers
references.note: Banks must prepare systems, procedures and policies to link with open banking providers under the framework technical standards.

references.title: SAMA Issues the Open Banking Framework
references.note: Announces the framework, with account information services first and payment initiation next.

references.title: SAMA Commences Licensing of Fintech Companies to Provide Open Banking Services
references.note: SAMA started licensing fintechs for open banking after the sandbox phase.

programs.title: Saudi Arabia | Fintech Innovation and the SAMA Regulatory Sandbox
programs.why: The refreshed SAMA Regulatory Sandbox Framework is open to licensed financial institutions as well as start-ups for live testing of innovative products under set controls and timeframes. Awareness is good practice for banks that test new products or partner with fintechs; no training obligation was found.

references.title: Regulatory Sandbox Framework
references.note: Describes the live testing environment open to licensed institutions and start-ups, with objectives and eligibility.

notes: SAMA issued new Rules for the Implementation of Targeted Financial Sanctions on 7 December 2025, with a dedicated training and awareness chapter, and Guidance on Assessing Business Risks covering ML, TF and proliferation financing on 31 December 2025.

Press and law-firm reports say the Council of Ministers approved amendments to the 2017 Anti-Money Laundering Law in April 2026 (penalties, travel bans, confiscation and the role of the Permanent Committee). The official text on laws.boe.gov.sa could not be opened, and the SAMA Rulebook copy did not yet show the amendment.

SAMA's 2012 AML/CTF Rules for banks and money exchangers are superseded; the AML/CTF Guide (circular 18318/486 of November 2019) is the current SAMA instrument, and it cites the 2017 AML Law, the CTF Law (amended 2020) and their implementing regulations.

The Personal Data Protection Law (amended by Royal Decree M/148 of 1444H) took effect on 14 September 2023 with a one-year grace period to September 2024; its implementing regulation and data transfer regulation were issued by SDAIA in 2023.

SAMA's Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements took effect on 13 April 2026 for finance companies and payment service providers (replacing the Anti-Fraud Rules for Finance Companies); banks remain under the 2022 Counter-Fraud Framework.
The Key Principles of Governance were reissued as version 2 in May 2024, and a December 2025 circular extends them to finance companies and payment service providers by 1448H.
SAMA consulted on a new Banking Law in 2023 to replace the 1966 Banking Control Law; no enacted replacement was confirmed, and the Rulebook still lists the Banking Control Law as in force.
Hosts laws.boe.gov.sa, sdaia.gov.sa, cma.org.sa, safiu.gov.sa, zatca.gov.sa and hrsd.gov.sa refused automated access; SAMA Rulebook copies of laws were used where available.

Banking circulars in 2025-2026 include new Rules of Issuance and Operation of Credit Cards (June 2025), technical amendments to the Basel III reforms (August 2025), updated IRRBB standardised shock scenarios (October 2025), the launch of the Electronic Cheque Clearing System (December 2025), the 2026 D-SIB list (March 2026) and several Account Opening Rules amendments (2025-2026).

Open banking: SAMA issued the Open Banking Framework in November 2022, began licensing fintechs for open banking in March 2026 and, at a September 2026 forum, focused on bank readiness for payment initiation services.
